source_refs.note: Exercise 12.2, Question 1 (i)-(iii): left and right hand limits and the limit as x -> c (book p.233). Answer key PDF 310 agrees.

blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Determine the left hand limit and the right hand limit and then, find limit of the following functions when \(x \to c\). \(f(x) = 2x^2 + x - 5,\ c = 1\)
blocks.explanation:
A one-sided limits question for a polynomial.
We must find the left hand limit (LHL), the right hand limit (RHL) and then the limit at \(x = 1\).
Plan: a polynomial has one formula on both sides, so substitute \(x = 1\) for each side and compare.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 2x^2 + x - 5\), \(c = 1\).
To find: \(\lim_{x \to 1^-} f(x)\), \(\lim_{x \to 1^+} f(x)\) and \(\lim_{x \to 1} f(x)\).
Method: For a polynomial, the limit is found by direct substitution (theorems on limits). The limit exists only if LHL = RHL.

Left hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to 1^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 1^-} (2x^2 + x - 5)\]
\[= 2(1)^2 + 1 - 5\]
\[= 2 + 1 - 5 = -2\]
Why: \(x \to 1^-\) means \(x\) comes to 1 through values a little less than 1 (0.9, 0.99, ...). The same formula is used there, and a polynomial has no break, so we may substitute \(x = 1\).

Right hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to 1^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 1^+} (2x^2 + x - 5)\]
\[= 2(1)^2 + 1 - 5 = -2\]
Why: From the right (1.1, 1.01, ...) the formula is the same, so the value is the same.

Compare and write the limit
\[\text{LHL} = \text{RHL} = -2\]
\[\lim_{x \to 1} f(x) = -2\]
Why: The limit of a function at a point exists exactly when both one-sided limits exist and are equal.

Check
\[f(0.99) = 1.9602 + 0.99 - 5 = -2.0498\]
\[f(1.01) = 2.0402 + 1.01 - 5 = -1.9498\]
Why: Values just left and just right of 1 are both close to \(-2\), as the limit says.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Determine the left hand limit and the right hand limit and then, find limit of the following functions when \(x \to c\). \(f(x) = \frac{x^2 - 9}{x - 3},\ c = -3\)
blocks.explanation:
A one-sided limits question for a rational function.
We must find the LHL, the RHL and the limit at \(x = -3\).
Plan: simplify the fraction by factorising, then substitute \(x = -3\) from each side.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = \dfrac{x^2 - 9}{x - 3}\), \(c = -3\).
To find: LHL, RHL and \(\lim_{x \to -3} f(x)\).
Method: Factorise \(x^2 - 9\) and cancel \(x - 3\) (allowed because near \(x = -3\) we have \(x \ne 3\)). The simplified form is a polynomial, so substitute.

Simplify the function
\[x^2 - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3)\]
\[f(x) = \frac{(x - 3)(x + 3)}{x - 3}\]
\[= x + 3 \quad (x \ne 3)\]
Why: Difference of squares, \(a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)\). Near \(-3\) the factor \(x - 3\) is about \(-6\), never zero, so it may be cancelled.

Left hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to -3^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to -3^-} (x + 3)\]
\[= -3 + 3 = 0\]
Why: Just left of \(-3\) (like \(-3.01\)) the simplified formula \(x + 3\) holds; substitute.

Right hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to -3^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to -3^+} (x + 3)\]
\[= -3 + 3 = 0\]
Why: Just right of \(-3\) (like \(-2.99\)) the same formula holds.

Compare and write the limit
\[\text{LHL} = \text{RHL} = 0\]
\[\lim_{x \to -3} f(x) = 0\]
Why: Equal one-sided limits give the limit.

Check
\[f(-3) = \frac{9 - 9}{-3 - 3} = \frac{0}{-6} = 0\]
Why: Here the function is even defined at \(-3\), and its value 0 agrees with the limit. (The fraction is undefined only at \(x = 3\), which is not our point.)

blocks.prompt: 1 (iii) Determine the left hand limit and the right hand limit and then, find limit of the following functions when \(x \to c\). \(f(x) = |x - 5|,\ c = 5\)
blocks.explanation:
A one-sided limits question with an absolute value.
We must find the LHL, the RHL and the limit at \(x = 5\).
Plan: remove the modulus separately on each side of 5, then substitute.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = |x - 5|\), \(c = 5\).
To find: LHL, RHL and \(\lim_{x \to 5} f(x)\).
Method: \(|a| = a\) when \(a \ge 0\) and \(|a| = -a\) when \(a < 0\). The sign of \(x - 5\) changes at 5, so each side gets its own formula.

Write \(f\) without the modulus
\[f(x) = \begin{cases} 5 - x, & x < 5 \\ x - 5, & x \ge 5 \end{cases}\]
Why: For \(x < 5\), \(x - 5\) is negative, so \(|x - 5| = -(x - 5) = 5 - x\). For \(x \ge 5\) it is not negative, so the modulus changes nothing.

Left hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to 5^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 5^-} (5 - x)\]
\[= 5 - 5 = 0\]
Why: Left of 5 (4.9, 4.99, ...) the formula is \(5 - x\).

Right hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to 5^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 5^+} (x - 5)\]
\[= 5 - 5 = 0\]
Why: Right of 5 (5.1, 5.01, ...) the formula is \(x - 5\).

Compare and write the limit
\[\text{LHL} = \text{RHL} = 0\]
\[\lim_{x \to 5} f(x) = 0\]
Why: Equal one-sided limits, so the limit exists.

Check
\[f(4.99) = |{-0.01}| = 0.01\]
\[f(5.01) = |0.01| = 0.01\]
Why: Both sides give values close to 0. The graph is a V shape with its corner at \((5, 0)\): a corner is not a break.
